analysis.title: Gold Miners Remain Resilient Despite Tighter Margins in Q2'26
key_insights: Global average gold producer AISC rose 8% q/q and 22% y/y to a record US$1,930/oz in Q2'26, the 29th consecutive year-on-year increase.

Sustaining capex was the main driver of higher AISC, up 34% q/q and 25% y/y to a record US$441/oz. It accounted for about 80% of the US$139/oz q/q net rise in AISC and lifted sustaining capital's share of the cost base to 23% from 18% in Q1'26.

Sustaining capex increases were concentrated in a minority of operations. Deferred spending timing amplified quarterly swings in unit costs without necessarily raising annual expenditure by the same amount.

Operational disruption added to costs at some mines. B2Gold's Goose mine had a crushing circuit fire and catch-up spending, taking AISC to US$6,390/oz. Newmont's Cadia was down after an April seismic event and returned to normal operations in mid-June.
Output at covered operations rose 1.6% q/q and grades improved 1.4%, but on an annual basis output fell 4.4% and grade fell 3.1%.
Cash Operating Costs rose 6% q/q and 18% y/y to US$1,215/oz. Total Cash Costs rose 4% q/q and 22% y/y to US$1,406/oz. Labour and diesel were the main pressures.

Agnico Eagle bought about 70% of its Nunavut diesel needs through the 2027 delivery season at prices about 30% above its 2026 budget, net of hedges. Westgold's higher diesel prices added A$12m to June-quarter costs.

Supply-chain constraints affected input availability as well as cost: Resolute reported logistics, fuel, reagent and explosives problems at Syama in Mali, and Evolution's Mungari had about three days of grid-power outages.

Royalty and production-tax costs fell 11% q/q to US$185/oz but were 53% higher y/y. Their share of AISC fell to 9.6% from 11.6%. Newmont reported a full quarter of Ghana's higher royalties. Corporate G&A fell 21% q/q to US$82/oz.
The average gold price fell 7.2% q/q to US$4,512/oz. Average AISC margin fell 16% q/q to US$2,582/oz, the second highest in the dataset. Gold was 37% higher y/y and margins 52% higher y/y.

Free cash flow was strong at AngloGold Ashanti (US$727m, +36% y/y) and Kinross (US$727m attributable, +12% y/y). Endeavour Mining's FCF fell to US$149m from US$613m on higher tax, lower realised prices, higher costs and greater investing outflows.
Miners kept returning cash: OceanaGold returned US$78m (US$58m buybacks) despite FCF falling to US$130m from US$255m. Endeavour paid about US$200m in dividends and repurchased US$42m of shares.
Balance sheets are strong. AngloGold repurchased about US$666m of bonds and ended June with US$991m net cash. Newmont, Agnico Eagle and Kinross reported net cash of US$3.4bn, US$3.3bn and US$1.9bn.

Outlook: with AISC approaching US$2,000/oz, fuel, supply-chain and inflation pressures should keep costs rising. Gold averaged US$4,266/oz in Q3'26 (down 5.5% q/q) and was about US$4,040/oz at the time of writing, which points to further margin contraction in the rest of 2026. A forecast gold price recovery in 2027 would raise royalties but widen margins on higher revenue.

sector_views.rationale: Margins are contracting from record levels as costs rise and prices fall, but cash generation and balance sheets remain strong. Further margin contraction is expected through the rest of 2026, with wider margins forecast in 2027.

earnings_insights: Agnico Eagle Q2 2026 results: sustaining expenditure rose 21% q/q to US$237m, mostly at Detour Lake and Fosterville.
AngloGold Ashanti Q2 2026 reported free cash flow of US$727m, up 36% y/y, and net cash of US$991m at end of June.
Kinross Q2 2026 reported attributable free cash flow of US$727m, up 12% y/y, and net cash of US$1.9bn at end of June.

Endeavour Mining reported free cash flow of US$149m, down from US$613m the prior quarter, and net cash of US$254m. The report labels this period 'H2'26', which appears to be a typo for H1'26 given the cited H1 2026 results.
OceanaGold Q2 2026 free cash flow was US$130m versus US$255m in Q1, with US$78m returned to shareholders including US$58m of buybacks.
B2Gold's Goose mine AISC reached US$6,390/oz in Q2 2026 after a crushing circuit fire and deferred catch-up spending.
Newmont Q2 2026 reported net cash of US$3.4bn, extra downtime costs at Cadia and a full quarter of Ghana's higher royalties.
Westgold Resources June 2026 quarter: higher diesel prices added A$12m to costs.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down 7.2% q/q and up 37% y/y, which compressed miner margins from Q1'26 levels.
Down 5.5% q/q, which points to further margin contraction.

macro_indicators.indicator: Gold price (spot at time of writing)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Below the Q2 and Q3 averages, which adds to margin pressure as costs rise.
A record, up 8% q/q and 22% y/y.
Down 16% q/q, up 52% y/y and the second highest in the dataset.

risk_factors: Further AISC increases as the cost approaches US$2,000/oz.
Diesel and fuel replenishment at higher prices after hedges and contracts roll off.
Supply-chain and logistics constraints on consumables, explosives and reagents.
Operational disruption such as fires and seismic events.
Gold price declines from the Q2 average, with spot at about US$4,040/oz.
Fiscal changes such as higher royalties, which persist when prices fall.
charts_described: Chart 1 is an AISC bridge from US$1,790/oz in Q1'26 to US$1,930/oz in Q2'26: cash operating cost +72, royalty costs -22, corporate G&A -22, sustaining capex +111.
Chart 2 plots AISC, AISC margins and the gold price from Q2'16 to Q2'26, and the report says margins have contracted with climbing costs and subdued prices but remain historically high.
geopolitical: Ghana's increased royalties fully affected Newmont in Q2'26.
Supply and logistics disruption at Syama in Mali affected Resolute Mining.

tension_points.bull_case: Q2'26 AISC margin of US$2,582/oz was the second highest in the dataset, up 52% y/y. Free cash flow, buybacks and net cash positions (Newmont US$3.4bn, Agnico Eagle US$3.3bn, Kinross US$1.9bn) leave a substantial cushion. A forecast gold price recovery in 2027 should widen margins.
tension_points.bear_case: AISC is approaching US$2,000/oz with fuel, supply-chain and inflation pressures expected to continue. The gold price averaged US$4,266/oz in Q3'26 and was about US$4,040/oz at writing, so margins are expected to contract further over the rest of 2026.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A gold price recovery in 2027, which the report forecasts would more than offset higher royalty costs and widen margins.

theme_stances.key_argument: Rising costs and lower gold prices will contract margins further in the rest of 2026, but strong balance sheets and cash generation limit the damage.
theme_stances.evidence: a retreat from exceptional margins rather than a collapse in cash generation
